subproblem.title: Blow-ups of a current equal to c[[ℝⁿ]] on a ball, and of local boundary vanishing
subproblem.statement: Let m ∈ ℕ, n := m + 1, U ⊆ ℝⁿ, T ∈ 𝒟_n(U), x ∈ ℝⁿ, ρ, c ∈ ℝ and λ > 0 with B_ρ(x) ⊆ U; let η := η_{x,λ} = dilation x λ (η(y) = λ⁻¹(y − x)) and S := η_{x,λ#}T = blowUp T x λ ∈ 𝒟_n(η(U)); e = standard basis of ℝⁿ. (i) If T(ω) = c·∫ω(y)(e) dy for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ B_ρ(x), then currentEval(S, ω) = c·∫ω(z)(e) dz for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(ℝⁿ) with tsupport ω ⊆ B_{ρ/λ}(0). (ii) If ∂T(β) = 0 for every β ∈ 𝒟^m(U) with tsupport β ⊆ B_ρ(x), then ∂S(β) = 0 for every β ∈ 𝒟^m(η(U)) with tsupport β ⊆ B_{ρ/λ}(0).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (m : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid (m + 1))) (T : GeometricCurrentOn U (m + 1)) (x : Euclid (m + 1)) (ρ c lam : ℝ) (hlam : 0 < lam), ball x ρ ⊆ U → ((∀ ω : TestFormOn U (m + 1), tsupport (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid (m + 1)) (m + 1)) ⊆ ball x ρ → T ω = c * ∫ y, (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid (m + 1)) (m + 1)) y ⇑(EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin (m + 1)) ℝ)) → ∀ ω : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Euclid (m + 1))) (m + 1), tsupport (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid (m + 1)) (m + 1)) ⊆ ball 0 (ρ / lam) → currentEval (blowUp T x lam hlam.ne') (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid (m + 1)) (m + 1)) = c * ∫ z, (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid (m + 1)) (m + 1)) z ⇑(EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin (m + 1)) ℝ)) ∧ ((∀ β : TestFormOn U m, tsupport (β : DifferentialForm (Euclid (m + 1)) m) ⊆ ball x ρ → T.boundary β = 0) → ∀ β : TestFormOn (dilation x lam '' U) m, tsupport (β : DifferentialForm (Euclid (m + 1)) m) ⊆ ball 0 (ρ / lam) → (blowUp T x lam hlam.ne').boundary β = 0)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: steps 5 and 7 of the parent proof of dtc_bc_codim_zero (the blow-ups agree with c[[ℝⁿ]] on the balls B_{ρ/λ}(0) by the change of variables y = x + λz; ∂S = ∂T(η^#·) vanishes there), with details filled in. No sibling is used.
Notation: e := ⇑(EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin n) ℝ); L := dilationCLM n λ = λ⁻¹·id; b := −(λ⁻¹·x); η(y) := dilation x λ y = b + L y = λ⁻¹(y − x). For a k-form ω on ℝⁿ, η^#ω := affinePullbackForm L b ω, (η^#ω)(y) = ω(η(y)) ∘ L, i.e. (η^#ω)(y)(v₁, …, v_k) = ω(η(y))(λ⁻¹v₁, …, λ⁻¹v_k).
1. Unfolding blowUp. By definition blowUp T x λ = (T.restrictDomain h).affinePushforward L b hproper, with h : η⁻¹(η(U)) ⊆ U. By GeometricCurrentOn.affinePushforward_apply and GeometricCurrentOn.restrictDomain_apply, for every ω ∈ TestFormOn (η(U)) n: S(ω) = T(ω♯), where ω♯ ∈ TestFormOn U n is the test form whose underlying form is η^#ω (affinePullbackTestOn followed by testFormOnInclusion h).
2. Balls. η is a bijection of ℝⁿ with inverse z ↦ x + λz, and ‖η(y)‖ = λ⁻¹‖y − x‖. Hence η⁻¹(B_{ρ/λ}(0)) = B_ρ(x) and η(B_ρ(x)) = B_{ρ/λ}(0); in particular B_{ρ/λ}(0) ⊆ η(U).
3. Supports. tsupport(η^#ω) ⊆ η⁻¹(tsupport ω) (tsupport_affinePullbackForm_subset). So tsupport ω ⊆ B_{ρ/λ}(0) implies tsupport(η^#ω) ⊆ B_ρ(x).
4. Pullback on e. By multilinearity, (η^#ω)(y)(e) = ω(η(y))(λ⁻¹e₁, …, λ⁻¹eₙ) = λ^{−n}·ω(η(y))(e) (ContinuousAlternatingMap.map_smul_univ; ∏_{i<n} λ⁻¹ = λ^{−n}).
5. Change of variables. For F : ℝⁿ → ℝ, ∫ F(η(y)) dy = λⁿ·∫ F(z) dz: F(η(y)) = F(λ⁻¹·(y − x)); translation invariance of Lebesgue measure (integral_sub_right_eq_self) gives ∫ F(λ⁻¹(y − x)) dy = ∫ F(λ⁻¹y) dy, and Measure.integral_comp_inv_smul_of_nonneg (λ ≥ 0; finrank ℝⁿ = n by finrank_euclideanSpace_fin) gives ∫ F(λ⁻¹y) dy = λⁿ·∫ F(z) dz. (No integrability assumption is needed.)
6. Proof of (i). Let ω ∈ TestFormOn univ n with tsupport ω ⊆ B_{ρ/λ}(0). Then ω is a test form with tsupport ω ⊆ η(U) (step 2), so by the definition of currentEval (its dite condition holds) currentEval(S, ω) = S(ω'), where ω' ∈ TestFormOn (η(U)) n has underlying form ω. By step 1, S(ω') = T(ω'♯), and the underlying form η^#ω of ω'♯ has tsupport ⊆ B_ρ(x) (step 3). By the hypothesis of (i), then step 4 and step 5 with F(z) := ω(z)(e): T(ω'♯) = c·∫ (η^#ω)(y)(e) dy = c·λ^{−n}·∫ ω(η(y))(e) dy = c·λ^{−n}·λⁿ·∫ ω(z)(e) dz = c·∫ ω(z)(e) dz.
7. Proof of (ii). Let β ∈ TestFormOn (η(U)) m with tsupport β ⊆ B_{ρ/λ}(0). By GeometricCurrentOn.boundary_apply, ∂S(β) = S(β₁), where β₁ := exteriorDerivativeTestOn (η(U)) m β has underlying form dβ. By step 1, S(β₁) = T(ζ), where ζ ∈ TestFormOn U n has underlying form η^#(dβ). By SimonGMT exteriorDerivative_affinePullbackForm, η^#(dβ) = d(η^#β); hence ζ = exteriorDerivativeTestOn U m β♯, where β♯ ∈ TestFormOn U m has underlying form η^#β (equality of test forms by Subtype.ext). [Equivalently: GeometricCurrentOn.boundary_affinePushforward, plus the fact that boundary commutes with restrictDomain, which holds by definition.] Thus ∂S(β) = T(dβ♯) = ∂T(β♯). Finally tsupport(η^#β) ⊆ η⁻¹(tsupport β) ⊆ B_ρ(x) (step 3), so ∂T(β♯) = 0 by the hypothesis of (ii). ∎

subproblem.title: Eventual agreement on balls gives weak convergence, convergence of mass measures and ∂C = 0
subproblem.statement: Assume measure locality (MEAS, the exact type of dtc_bc_measure_restrict_eq_of_eqOn, taken as a hypothesis): for all P, n, open U₁, U₂, W ⊆ ℝ^P with W ⊆ U₁ ∩ U₂, T₁ ∈ 𝒟_n(U₁), T₂ ∈ 𝒟_n(U₂) and integer multiplicity representations R₁ of T₁, R₂ of T₂, if currentEval T₁ ω = currentEval T₂ ω for every ω ∈ TestFormOn W n then R₁.measure.restrict W = R₂.measure.restrict W. Let P, m ∈ ℕ, n := m + 1, U_j ⊆ ℝ^P open (j ∈ ℕ), S_j ∈ 𝒟_n(U_j), and C ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P). Assume that for every R ∈ ℝ, for all sufficiently large j: B_R(0) ⊆ U_j; currentEval(S_j, ω) = C(ω) for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(ℝ^P) with tsupport ω ⊆ B_R(0); and ∂S_j(β) = 0 for every β ∈ 𝒟^m(U_j) with tsupport β ⊆ B_R(0). Then S_j ⇀ C in ℝ^P (ConvergesWeakly), μ_{S_j} → μ_C for all integer multiplicity representations (MassMeasuresConverge), and ∂C = 0 (C.boundary = 0).
subproblem.lean_statement: (∀ (P n : ℕ) (U₁ U₂ W : Set (Euclid P)) (T₁ : GeometricCurrentOn U₁ n) (T₂ : GeometricCurrentOn U₂ n) (R₁ : IMRep U₁ n) (R₂ : IMRep U₂ n), IsOpen U₁ → IsOpen U₂ → IsOpen W → W ⊆ U₁ → W ⊆ U₂ → R₁.Represents T₁ → R₂.Represents T₂ → (∀ ω : TestFormOn W n, currentEval T₁ (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) = currentEval T₂ (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n)) → R₁.measure.restrict W = R₂.measure.restrict W) → ∀ (P m : ℕ) (Us : ℕ → Set (Euclid P)) (Ss : (j : ℕ) → GeometricCurrentOn (Us j) (m + 1)) (C : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) (m + 1)), (∀ j, IsOpen (Us j)) → (∀ R : ℝ, ∀ᶠ j in atTop, ball (0 : Euclid P) R ⊆ Us j ∧ (∀ ω : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) (m + 1), tsupport (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) (m + 1)) ⊆ ball 0 R → currentEval (Ss j) (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) (m + 1)) = C ω) ∧ ∀ β : TestFormOn (Us j) m, tsupport (β : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) m) ⊆ ball 0 R → (Ss j).boundary β = 0) → ConvergesWeakly Ss C ∧ MassMeasuresConverge Ss C ∧ C.boundary = 0
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: steps 6, 7 and 8 of the parent proof of dtc_bc_codim_zero (every test form is eventually supported in a ball on which S_j = C; measure locality; the boundary of the limit), stated for a general sequence. Measure locality is the leading hypothesis (MEAS) of this lemma: its type is exactly that of dtc_bc_measure_restrict_eq_of_eqOn, the resolved dependency of the parent node, which the parent passes in (that declaration is not accepted yet and is owned by another parent, so it cannot be listed as a sibling here). No sibling is used.
0. Every compact K ⊆ ℝ^P is bounded, hence K ⊆ B_R(0) for some R (IsCompact.isBounded, Bornology.IsBounded.subset_ball). In particular every test form ω satisfies tsupport ω ⊆ B_R(0) for some R (its tsupport is compact).
1. ConvergesWeakly. Let ω ∈ TestFormOn univ n and choose R with tsupport ω ⊆ B_R(0) (step 0). By hypothesis, currentEval(S_j, ω) = C(ω) for all large j. A sequence that is eventually equal to C(ω) converges to C(ω) (tendsto_const_nhds.congr').
2. MassMeasuresConverge. Let R_j : IMRep U_j n represent S_j, R : IMRep univ n represent C, and f : ℝ^P → ℝ be continuous with compact support. Choose R₀ with tsupport f ⊆ W := B_{R₀}(0) (step 0), and let j be large enough that the hypothesis holds with R := R₀. For ω ∈ TestFormOn W n, the underlying form is a test form with tsupport ⊆ W ⊆ univ; regarding it as an element ω̄ of TestFormOn univ n, the hypothesis gives currentEval(S_j, ω) = C(ω̄), and C(ω̄) = currentEval(C, ω) by the definition of currentEval (its dite condition holds since the domain of C is univ). So MEAS applies with U₁ := U_j, U₂ := univ, W, T₁ := S_j, T₂ := C, R₁ := R_j, R₂ := R (U_j, univ and W are open; W ⊆ U_j; W ⊆ univ) and gives R_j.measure.restrict W = R.measure.restrict W. Since f = 0 outside W (outside tsupport f), ∫ f dR_j.measure = ∫_W f dR_j.measure = ∫_W f dR.measure = ∫ f dR.measure (setIntegral_eq_integral_of_forall_compl_eq_zero for each of the two measures, and the equality of the restricted measures; no integrability is needed). So j ↦ ∫ f dR_j.measure is eventually equal to ∫ f dR.measure, hence converges to it.
3. ∂C = 0. Let β ∈ TestFormOn univ m; choose R with tsupport β ⊆ B_R(0) and one index j for which the three hypotheses hold with this R (the hypothesis holds eventually, so such j exists). The form dβ is a test form with tsupport dβ ⊆ tsupport β ⊆ B_R(0) (exteriorDerivative_isTestForm, tsupport_exteriorDerivative_subset). Then C.boundary β = C(dβ) (GeometricCurrentOn.boundary_apply) = currentEval(S_j, dβ) (second hypothesis) = S_j(dβ'), where dβ' ∈ TestFormOn U_j n has underlying form dβ (definition of currentEval; tsupport dβ ⊆ B_R(0) ⊆ U_j). Since tsupport β ⊆ B_R(0) ⊆ U_j, β defines β' ∈ TestFormOn U_j m, and exteriorDerivativeTestOn U_j m β' = dβ' (same underlying form; Subtype.ext); so S_j(dβ') = S_j.boundary β' = 0 by the third hypothesis. Hence C.boundary β = 0 for every β, i.e. C.boundary = 0 (GeometricCurrentOn.ext). ∎

proof_key_steps: Each test form (and each f ∈ C_c) is supported in some ball B_R(0); on that ball S_j agrees with C for all large j, so currentEval(S_j, ω) is eventually C(ω).
For large j, the hypothesis MEAS on W = B_R(0) gives R_j.measure⌞W = R.measure⌞W, so ∫ f dμ_{R_j} = ∫ f dμ_R eventually.
C(dβ) = currentEval(S_j, dβ) = ∂S_j(β) = 0 for large j, so ∂C = 0.

subproblem.statement: Let n ≥ 1, V ⊆ ℝⁿ open and X ∈ 𝒟_n(V) (GeometricCurrentOn V n) integer multiplicity (IsIntegerMultiplicity X). Let e = (e₁, …, eₙ) be the standard basis of ℝⁿ (EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin n) ℝ) and, for an n-covector α, write α(e) := α(e₁, …, eₙ). Then there is g : ℝⁿ → ℤ such that y ↦ (g(y) : ℝ) is locally Lebesgue-integrable on V (LocallyIntegrableOn (fun y => (g y : ℝ)) V volume) and X(ω) = ∫_{ℝⁿ} g(y)·ω(y)(e) dLⁿ(y) for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(V) (TestFormOn V n).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n : ℕ) (V : Set (Euclid n)) (X : GeometricCurrentOn V n), 0 < n → IsOpen V → IsIntegerMultiplicity X → ∃ g : Euclid n → ℤ, LocallyIntegrableOn (fun y => (g y : ℝ)) V volume ∧ ∀ ω : TestFormOn V n, X ω = ∫ y, (g y : ℝ) * (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid n) n) y ⇑(EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin n) ℝ)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Lemma A (step 1) of the parent proof of dtc_bc_codim_zero — the density part of the Constancy Theorem (Simon Ch. 6, 2.34, chapter-06.txt lines 571–600), specialized to integer multiplicity currents — with all details filled in. No sibling is used.
Notation. Hⁿ := μHE[n] and Lⁿ := volume on ℝⁿ = Euclid n; Mathlib EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume n gives Hⁿ = Lⁿ. b := EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin n) ℝ (an orthonormal basis), e := ⇑b, and D := b.toBasis.det, the alternating n-linear form with D(e) = 1 (Module.Basis.det_self). D is continuous (D(v) is the determinant of the coordinate matrix of v, Module.Basis.det_apply, a continuous function of v by Continuous.matrix_det), so D defines an n-covector e* ∈ Covector (Euclid n) n with e*(v) = D(v) and e*(e) = 1.
1. Fix R = (M, θ, ξ) : IMRep V n with R.Represents X (definition of IsIntegerMultiplicity). Thus X(ω) = ∫_M θ(y)·ξ(y)(ω(y)) dHⁿ(y) for every ω ∈ TestFormOn V n (IMRep.action); M is a measurable subset of V; θ : ℝⁿ → ℕ is measurable with ∫⁻_{M∩K} θ dHⁿ < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ V (field locallyIntegrable_mult); ξ is AEStronglyMeasurable for Hⁿ⌞M.
2. Every n-covector α satisfies α(v) = α(e)·D(v) for all v : Fin n → ℝⁿ: apply Mathlib AlternatingMap.eq_smul_basis_det to the alternating map underlying α and the basis b.toBasis.
3. Let y ∈ M be a point at which the `orients` property of R holds (this is the case for Hⁿ⌞M-a.e. y): there is a subspace Q with HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M y Q and IsUnitOrientationOf (ξ(y)) Q. The first gives finrank Q = n (HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt.finrank_eq) = finrank ℝⁿ, so Q = ⊤ (Submodule.eq_top_of_finrank_eq). The second gives an orthonormal τ : Fin n → ℝⁿ with span(range τ) = Q = ⊤ such that either ξ(y)(α) = α(τ) for all α, or ξ(y)(α) = −α(τ) for all α. Since τ is orthonormal and spans ⊤, it is an orthonormal basis (OrthonormalBasis.mk with OrthonormalBasis.coe_mk), and the change-of-basis determinant between two orthonormal bases is ±1 (Mathlib OrthonormalBasis.det_to_matrix_orthonormalBasis_real); thus D(τ) = b.toBasis.det τ ∈ {1, −1}. By step 2, α(τ) = α(e)·D(τ). Hence there is s(y) ∈ {1, −1} with ξ(y)(α) = s(y)·α(e) for every α; taking α = e* gives s(y) = ξ(y)(e*).

By step 3, for Hⁿ⌞M-a.e. y: σ(y) ∈ {1, −1} and ξ(y)(α) = σ(y)·α(e) for every n-covector α. σ is the composition of ξ with the continuous linear map "evaluation at e*" (ContinuousLinearMap.apply ℝ ℝ e*), hence AEStronglyMeasurable for Hⁿ⌞M; let σ̃ be a measurable function with σ̃ = σ Hⁿ⌞M-a.e. (AEStronglyMeasurable.mk).
5. Define g : ℝⁿ → ℤ by g(y) := θ(y) if y ∈ M and σ̃(y) ≥ 0; g(y) := −θ(y) if y ∈ M and σ̃(y) < 0; g(y) := 0 if y ∉ M. Since V is open (hence locally closed), integrability on every compact subset of V is equivalent to LocallyIntegrableOn (fun y => (g y : ℝ)) V volume (locallyIntegrableOn_iff with hV.isLocallyClosed).

Because g = 0 outside M, ∫_M g·ω(e) dHⁿ = ∫_{ℝⁿ} g·ω(e) dHⁿ (setIntegral_eq_integral_of_forall_compl_eq_zero), and Hⁿ = Lⁿ turns this into X(ω) = ∫ g(y)·ω(y)(e) dLⁿ(y). subproblem.statement: Let n ≥ 1 and c ∈ ℤ. 1. For ω ∈ TestFormOn univ n put F_ω(y) := ω(y)(e). F_ω is continuous (ω is smooth, in particular continuous, and evaluation of a continuous alternating map at the fixed tuple e is a continuous linear map) and vanishes outside tsupport ω, which is compact; hence F_ω is continuous with compact support and Lⁿ-integrable (Continuous.integrable_of_hasCompactSupport). Moreover |F_ω(y)| ≤ ‖ω(y)‖·∏_i ‖e_i‖ = ‖ω(y)‖ (ContinuousAlternatingMap.le_opNorm).
2. Define Λ(ω) := c·∫ F_ω dLⁿ. Since F_{ω+η} = F_ω + F_η and F_{tω} = t·F_ω, and these functions are integrable (step 1), Λ is ℝ-linear (integral_add, integral_smul): Λ : TestFormOn univ n →ₗ[ℝ] ℝ.
3. Continuity (the field continuous' of GeometricCurrentOn). Let (ω_q) satisfy TestFormOnConverges ω_q 0: there is a compact K with tsupport ω_q ⊆ K for all q, and iteratedFDeriv ℝ 0 ω_q → iteratedFDeriv ℝ 0 0 = 0 uniformly on K. As ‖iteratedFDeriv ℝ 0 f y‖ = ‖f y‖ (norm_iteratedFDeriv_zero), for every ε > 0 and all large q we have ‖ω_q(y)‖ ≤ ε for y ∈ K, while ω_q(y) = 0 for y ∉ K. By step 1, |Λ(ω_q)| ≤ |c|·∫_K ‖ω_q(y)‖ dy ≤ |c|·Lⁿ(K)·ε for all large q, and Lⁿ(K) < ∞ since K is compact. Hence Λ(ω_q) → 0. Thus C := ⟨Λ, continuity⟩ ∈ GeometricCurrentOn univ n, and C(ω) = c·∫ ω(y)(e) dy.
4. Integer multiplicity, case c = 0. Then C(ω) = 0 for all ω. Let R₀ have carrier ∅, mult ≡ 0 and orient ≡ 0. The IMRep fields hold: ∅ is measurable and ∅ ⊆ univ; CountablyRectifiable n ∅ (Chapter03 countablyRectifiable_of_measure_zero, Hⁿ(∅) = 0); constant functions are measurable and AEStronglyMeasurable; mult_pos is vacuous; ∫⁻_{∅∩K} 0 dHⁿ = 0 ≠ ∞; Hⁿ⌞∅ = 0, so the `orients` property holds Hⁿ⌞∅-a.e. R₀.action ω = ∫ over ∅ = 0 = C(ω), so R₀ represents C.
5. Integer multiplicity, case c ≠ 0. Let ε : MultiVector n n = (Covector (Euclid n) n →L[ℝ] ℝ) be the evaluation α ↦ α(e); it is linear and |α(e)| ≤ ‖α‖ (step 1), so it is a continuous linear map (LinearMap.mkContinuous with constant 1). (c) mult is constant (measurable) and positive because c ≠ 0. (d) For compact K: ∫⁻_{univ∩K} |c| dHⁿ = |c|·Hⁿ(K) = |c|·Lⁿ(K) < ∞. (e) orient is constant, hence AEStronglyMeasurable. 6. Action: R.action ω = ∫_{univ} |c|·s·ω(y)(e) dHⁿ(y) = c·∫ ω(y)(e) dLⁿ(y) = C(ω) (Measure.restrict_univ, Hⁿ = Lⁿ, |c|·s = c, MeasureTheory.integral_const_mul). So R represents C and C is integer multiplicity. ∎

subproblem.title: Every integer multiplicity n-current in ℝⁿ is minimizing
subproblem.statement: Let n ≥ 1, C ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝⁿ) (GeometricCurrentOn univ n) integer multiplicity, and A ⊆ ℝⁿ an arbitrary set. Then C is minimizing in A (Simon 7.1.1, IsMinimizingIn C A). In fact every integer multiplicity S ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝⁿ) with ∂S = ∂C and spt(S − C) compact equals C.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n : ℕ) (C : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid n)) n) (A : Set (Euclid n)), 0 < n → IsIntegerMultiplicity C → IsMinimizingIn C A
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 9 of the parent proof of dtc_bc_codim_zero (minimality of C: a competitor differs from C by a compactly supported integer multiplicity cycle, which the Constancy Theorem forces to vanish), stated for an arbitrary integer multiplicity C and an arbitrary A (the argument never uses spt(S − C) ⊆ A ∩ W). Siblings used: top_constancy (Cst), im_sub (G = the accepted declaration dtc_isIntegerMultiplicity_sub) and vanish_off_support (V = the accepted declaration dtc_vanish_off_support).
1. Write n = m + 1. The first conjunct of IsMinimizingIn C A is IsIntegerMultiplicity C, a hypothesis.
2. Let W be open with CompactlyContained W univ, and let S ∈ GeometricCurrentOn univ n be integer multiplicity with SameBoundary S C (for n = m + 1 this unfolds to S.boundary = C.boundary), IsCompact (S − C).support and (S − C).support ⊆ A ∩ W. Put X := S − C; by the definition of subtraction of currents (toCurrent := S.toCurrent − C.toCurrent), X(ω) = S(ω) − C(ω) for every ω.
3. X is integer multiplicity by G (univ is open, n > 0, S and C are integer multiplicity).
4. ∂X = 0: for β ∈ TestFormOn univ m, X.boundary β = X(dβ) = S(dβ) − C(dβ) = S.boundary β − C.boundary β = 0 (GeometricCurrentOn.boundary_apply).
5. Apply Cst with V := B := univ (open; preconnected since ℝⁿ is convex, convex_univ.isPreconnected), X (step 3) and the hypothesis of step 4: there is c' ∈ ℤ with X(ω) = c'·∫ ω(y)(e) dy for every ω ∈ TestFormOn univ n (the condition tsupport ω ⊆ univ is automatic).
6. c' = 0. The set spt X = (S − C).support is compact, hence bounded: spt X ⊆ closedBall(0, r₀) for some r₀ ∈ ℝ (IsCompact.isBounded, Bornology.IsBounded.subset_closedBall). Let p := (|r₀| + 2)·e₁ (n ≥ 1; ‖p‖ = |r₀| + 2 since ‖e₁‖ = 1), and let a be the smooth bump function centred at p with inner radius 1/2 and outer radius 1 (ContDiffBump p): a is C^∞ (ContDiffBump.contDiff), a ≥ 0, HasCompactSupport a, tsupport a = closedBall(p, 1) (ContDiffBump.tsupport_eq), and ∫ a > 0 (ContDiffBump.integral_pos, from Mathlib.Analysis.Calculus.BumpFunction.Normed). Let e* be the n-covector v ↦ D(v), D := (EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin n) ℝ).toBasis.det (continuous because D(v) is the determinant of the coordinate matrix of v: Module.Basis.det_apply, Continuous.matrix_det; e*(e) = 1 by Module.Basis.det_self), and ω(y) := a(y)·e*. Then ω is smooth with compact support, so ω ∈ TestFormOn univ n, and tsupport ω ⊆ tsupport a = closedBall(p, 1) (tsupport_smul_subset_left). For y ∈ closedBall(p, 1), ‖y‖ ≥ ‖p‖ − ‖y − p‖ ≥ |r₀| + 1 > r₀, so tsupport ω is disjoint from closedBall(0, r₀) ⊇ spt X, and V gives X(ω) = 0. By step 5, X(ω) = c'·∫ a(y)·e*(e) dy = c'·∫ a. Since ∫ a > 0, c' = 0.
7. Hence X(ω) = 0, i.e. S(ω) = C(ω), for every ω ∈ TestFormOn univ n; so S = C (GeometricCurrentOn.ext), C.massOn W = S.massOn W, and in particular C.massOn W ≤ S.massOn W. This proves IsMinimizingIn C A. ∎
